{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Overloaded Day 1 visits with multiple procedures",
      "quote": "1 (Day 1)",
      "page": 56,
      "section": "8.1 Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Day 1 includes a large number of procedures: complete physical exam, ECG, vital signs, cemiplimab infusion, hematology/chemistry, urinalysis, aPTT/INR, RF/ANA, TSH/CRP, ADA, PK, and concomitant meds. This is burdensome for patients and staff.",
      "fix": "Consider moving some non-critical labs (e.g., RF/ANA, TSH/CRP) to a separate visit or to screening if baseline values are needed."
    },
    {
      "title": "Redundant PK sampling on Day 1 and Day 22",
      "quote": "Cemiplimab PK/Drug Conc",
      "page": 56,
      "section": "8.1 Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "PK samples are collected at every dosing visit (Day 1, 22, 43, 64) and at EOS. For a Q3W regimen, this may be more frequent than needed for population PK; could be reduced to sparse sampling.",
      "fix": "Reduce PK sampling to a subset of visits (e.g., Day 1, Day 43, EOS) to lessen patient burden."
    },
    {
      "title": "Tight window for Day 22 and Day 43 visits",
      "quote": "22± 3 (Day 22)",
      "page": 56,
      "section": "8.1 Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The ±3 day window for a Q3W regimen is very tight, especially for a 3-week cycle. This may be difficult for sites to schedule and could lead to many protocol deviations.",
      "fix": "Consider widening the window to ±7 days for visits after Day 1."
    },
    {
      "title": "Tumor biopsies at Day 22 may be difficult to collect",
      "quote": "Tumor biopsies for Group 218",
      "page": 56,
      "section": "8.1 Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "On-treatment biopsy at Day 22 is invasive and may be challenging for patients and sites, especially if the tumor is not easily accessible. This could lead to missing data.",
      "fix": "Consider making the on-treatment biopsy optional or allowing a window (e.g., Day 22 ±7) and providing clear guidance on acceptable biopsy sites."
    },
    {
      "title": "CT/MRI and/or digital photography at multiple visits may be excessive",
      "quote": "CT/MRI and/or digital photography",
      "page": 56,
      "section": "8.1 Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Imaging is scheduled at screening, Day 22, Day 43, and Day 64. For a 12-week treatment period, this is frequent and may be burdensome. Some imaging could be aligned with response assessments only.",
      "fix": "Reduce imaging frequency to align with key efficacy timepoints (e.g., Day 43 and EOS) unless clinically indicated."
    },
    {
      "title": "Serum HCG at screening with ≤72 hour predose requirement is logistically hard",
      "quote": "Serum HCG ≤72 Hour Predose",
      "page": 56,
      "section": "8.1 Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The requirement that serum HCG must be within 72 hours before first dose may be difficult to coordinate with the screening visit, especially if the first dose is not scheduled immediately after screening.",
      "fix": "Consider allowing a urine pregnancy test at screening and a serum HCG on Day 1 predose, or extend the window to 7 days."
    },
    {
      "title": "ADA sampling at Day 1 and Day 43 may miss treatment-boosted responses",
      "quote": "ADA",
      "page": 56,
      "section": "8.1 Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "ADA is collected at Day 1, Day 43, and EOS. For a 12-week treatment, sampling at Day 22 and Day 64 might be needed to capture early and late ADA responses, especially for treatment-boosted responses.",
      "fix": "Consider adding ADA at Day 22 and Day 64 to better characterize immunogenicity."
    },
    {
      "title": "End of Study visit includes many procedures that may be redundant",
      "quote": "End of Study 30 days after last dose cemiplimab 3",
      "page": 56,
      "section": "8.1 Schedule of Activities",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The EOS visit includes complete physical exam, ECG, vital signs, hematology/chemistry, urine pregnancy, urinalysis, aPTT/INR, RF/ANA, TSH/CRP, ADA, PK, and concomitant meds. This is a heavy burden for a safety follow-up visit.",
      "fix": "Consider reducing EOS labs to only those needed for safety (e.g., hematology/chemistry, urinalysis) and omit RF/ANA and TSH/CRP unless clinically indicated."
    }
  ]
}
